Executive Summary Key Takeaways - What this data tells you BMW N47D20C is the most replaced UK engine (1,450 requests) Timing chain failure affects BMW 4-cylinder diesels across multiple models. Land Rover engines occupy 4 of top 10 spots 204DTD, SDV6, 276DT, and 368DT - premium SUV owners face significant replacement risk. VW EA189 is #4 (1,050 requests) Despite Dieselgate, these engines are still failing; the used market is keeping them going. Recon fitted costs range from £1,590 to £13,300 Replacement cost varies by nearly 10x across the top 15 engines. Ford DV6 and Renault K9K are 🔴 Scrap Threshold engines Replacement often exceeds vehicle value for these models. 70.45% of requests are for reconditioned engines Warranty and documented quality are valued over upfront savings. Transparency Dataset Limitations & Understanding the data Replacement frequency ≠ unreliability: High volume may reflect large vehicle parc, not engineering quality. Self-reporting bias: Requests come from platform users, not a random sample. Age skew: Older vehicles (8+ years) are overrepresented. Commercial vehicles: Light commercial vehicles have different failure patterns and are not fully captured. Expert Advice Frequently Asked Questions What is the most replaced engine in the UK? + The BMW N47D20C is the most replaced engine in the UK, with 1,450 quote requests in 2025 [EM-VERIFIED] . This 2.0-litre diesel engine is found in BMW 3 Series, 1 Series, 5 Series, X1, and X3 models. The primary failure is timing chain stretch, particularly on the rear-mounted chain. Is the most replaced engine the most unreliable? + No. High replacement frequency may reflect large vehicle parc (many on the road), age profile, or audience bias - not engineering quality. For example, the VW EA189 2.0 TDI is #4 with 1,050 requests, partly because millions were sold in the UK. How much does it cost to replace a BMW N47 engine? + A reconditioned BMW N47D20C costs £3,200-£5,500 supply-only, or £3,850-£6,410 fitted [EM-QUOTE] . Used options start from £1,800-£3,200 supply-only. Fitting costs depend on your region and garage. Why are Land Rover engines so prominent in the top 15? + Land Rover engines occupy 4 of the top 10 spots (204DTD, 306DT SDV6, 276DT, 368DT). This is due to a combination of known engineering issues (timing chain tensioners, crankshaft bearings, oil pump housings), high vehicle values that justify replacement, and a large premium SUV parc in the UK. Is it worth replacing a Ford DV6 1.6 TDCi engine? + The Ford DV6 1.6 TDCi is flagged as a 🔴 Scrap Threshold engine. With fitted costs of £1,590-£2,720 and typical vehicle values of £1,200-£5,000, replacement often exceeds the car's value. Consider scrapping unless the car is in excellent condition. Why does reconditioned cost more than used? + Reconditioned engines are disassembled, cleaned, and have worn parts replaced (pistons, rings, bearings, seals). They are tested to standard and come with a 6-12 month warranty. Used engines are direct from donor vehicles with unknown history. What should I consider when deciding repair vs. scrap? + If the fitted replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, consider scrapping. However, rare, collectable, or sentimental vehicles may justify spending above this threshold. Check our engine replacement cost guide for more guidance. How can I get a personalised replacement quote? + Use the Get Your Personalised Price form at the top and bottom of this page. Enter your vehicle registration, and we'll connect you with 100+ UK specialist suppliers for real, no-obligation quotes. mainEntity.name: What is the most replaced engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW N47D20C is the most replaced engine in the UK, with 1,450 quote requests in 2025 [EM-VERIFIED]. This 2.0-litre diesel engine is found in BMW 3 Series, 1 Series, 5 Series, X1, and X3 models. The primary failure is timing chain stretch, particularly on the rear-mounted chain.

mainEntity.name: Is the most replaced engine the most unreliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. High replacement frequency may reflect large vehicle parc (many on the road), age profile, or audience bias - not engineering quality. For example, the VW EA189 2.0 TDI is #4 with 1,050 requests, partly because millions were sold in the UK.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a BMW N47 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned BMW N47D20C costs £3,200-£5,500 supply-only, or £3,850-£6,410 fitted. Used options start from £1,800-£3,200 supply-only. Fitting costs depend on your region and garage.

mainEntity.name: Why are Land Rover engines so prominent in the top 15?

acceptedAnswer.text: Land Rover engines occupy 4 of the top 10 spots due to known engineering issues, high vehicle values that justify replacement, and a large premium SUV parc in the UK.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing a Ford DV6 1.6 TDCi engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Ford DV6 1.6 TDCi is flagged as a Scrap Threshold engine. With fitted costs of £1,590-£2,720 and typical vehicle values of £1,200-£5,000, replacement often exceeds the car's value.

mainEntity.name: Why does reconditioned cost more than used?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reconditioned engines are disassembled, cleaned, and have worn parts replaced. They are tested to standard and come with a 6-12 month warranty. Used engines are direct from donor vehicles with unknown history.

mainEntity.name: What should I consider when deciding repair vs. scrap?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the fitted replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, consider scrapping. Rare, collectable, or sentimental vehicles may justify spending above this threshold.
